ferrox-front/architecture.title: Architecture Deep Dive
ferrox-front/architecture.description: Ferrox Front is engineered using system design principles and zero-cost abstractions to guarantee peak execution performance inside WebAssembly.

ferrox-front/components.title: Component Library & Interactive Playground
ferrox-front/components.description: Explore and interact with the Ferrox Front component library live in your browser using our Nivo-Style Interactive Playground.

ferrox-front/core.title: Ferrox Front Core Engine (ferrox-front-core)
ferrox-front/core.description: ferrox-front-core is the foundational engine of Ferrox Front. It houses the fine-grained Signals Reactivity Graph, the zero-copy Wasm DOM Builder, and the Glassmorphism Theme System.

ferrox-front/intro.title: Introduction to Ferrox Front
ferrox-front/intro.description: Ferrox Front is a native Rust UI framework compiled to WebAssembly (Wasm), designed for building Enterprise SaaS applications, high-performance real-time dashboards, and Zero-Trust micro-frontend architectures.

ferrox-front/macros.title: Procedural RSX Macro (ferrox-front-macro)
ferrox-front/macros.description: ferrox-front-macro provides the rsx! procedural macro, enabling JSX/HTML-like component syntax directly inside Rust code.

ferrox-front/overview.title: Overview
ferrox-front/overview.description: Ferrox Front is a high-performance, WebAssembly (WASM) based frontend framework written in Rust, leveraging the Yew framework under the hood. It provides a robust, type-safe environment for building complex User Interfaces while maintaining near-native performance.

ferrox-front/quickstart.title: Quickstart Guide
ferrox-front/quickstart.description: This guide demonstrates how to install prerequisites, build your first WebAssembly application in Rust using Ferrox Front, and run it in the browser.

ferrox-front/reactivity.title: Reactivity & Signals API
ferrox-front/reactivity.description: Signals represent the fundamental building block for state management in Ferrox Front.

ferrox-front/routing.title: SPA Routing & Micro-Frontends
ferrox-front/routing.description: ferrox-front-router provides client-side SPA routing backed by the browser History API without page reloads.

ferrox-front/security.title: Zero-Trust Security & E2EE
ferrox-front/security.description: In Ferrox Front, security is enforced directly inside WebAssembly bytecode, isolating application memory from browser-based script attacks. The ferrox-front-security crate provides a complete suite of Zero-Trust mechanisms: from memory anti-tampering to biometric passkeys.

ferrox-front/templates.title: SaaS Page Templates
ferrox-front/templates.description: ferrox-front-templates provides pre-built SaaS layouts to accelerate enterprise frontend development.

ferrox-front/ui-components.title: Glassmorphism Design System (ferrox-front-ui)
ferrox-front/ui-components.description: ferrox-front-ui provides a complete, enterprise-grade Glassmorphism Design System for WebAssembly applications. It includes Design Tokens, a 12-column responsive layout grid, a Virtualized DataGrid (1,000,000+ rows), and a comprehensive library of pre-styled UI components.

ferrox-front/ws.title: Real-Time WebSockets Engine (ferrox-front-ws)
ferrox-front/ws.description: ferrox-front-ws provides an asynchronous WebAssembly WebSocket client engine built natively for Rust frontends. It bridges browser WebSocket APIs (web_sys::WebSocket) with Ferrox Front's reactive Signals graph (Signal), enabling low-latency, real-time bi-directional streaming for dashboards, chat applications, financial tickers, and live notification systems.

ferrox-node/overview.title: Overview
ferrox-node/overview.description: Ferrox Node is the crucial bridge that connects the high-performance Rust core (ferrox) with the Node.js ecosystem (nestjs-yalc and node-yalc).

ferrox/abstractions/crud-generator.title: 🛠️ Code Factory & Generic CRUD Generator
ferrox/abstractions/crud-generator.description: Building standard CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) endpoints for dozens of entities generates massive amounts of repetitive boilerplate.

ferrox/abstractions/guards.title: 🛡️ Guards (Authorization)
ferrox/abstractions/guards.description: Guards have a single responsibility: they determine whether a given request will be handled by the route handler or not, depending on certain conditions (like permissions, roles, ACLs, etc.) present at run-time.

ferrox/abstractions/pipes.title: 🛑 Pipes (Validation)
ferrox/abstractions/pipes.description: In NestJS, a Pipe is a class annotated with @Injectable() that implements the PipeTransform interface, typically used to validate or transform input data before it reaches the Controller.

ferrox/abstractions/validation.title: 🎯 DTO Validation & AutoZod Extractor
ferrox/abstractions/validation.description: In NestJS, developer productivity relies heavily on class-validator and ValidationPipe. In Rust, ferrox-validation provides the ValidatedJson extractor—a mechanism that behaves like Zod's .parse().

ferrox/architectures/api-gateway.title: 🛡️ Zero-Trust API Gateway Pattern
ferrox/architectures/api-gateway.description: In enterprise microservice architectures, authenticating requests against a database across 50 separate microservices creates massive database connection bottlenecks and security perimeters.

ferrox/architectures/caching.title: ⚡ Caching & Stampede Protection
ferrox/architectures/caching.description: In high-traffic Enterprise applications, Caching is mandatory. However, caching introduces a catastrophic vulnerability known as a Cache Stampede (or Dog-Piling).

ferrox/architectures/cqrs.title: 🗃️ CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation)
ferrox/architectures/cqrs.description: CQRS is an architectural pattern that separates reading data (Queries) from writing data (Commands).

ferrox/architectures/events.title: 📡 Event-Driven Architecture & Event Bus
ferrox/architectures/events.description: Event-driven architecture decouples producers of business events from subscribers that react to them (e.g. sending welcome emails when a UserCreatedEvent fires, updating analytics counters, or invalidating caches).

ferrox/architectures/queues-jobs.title: 📬 Background Jobs & Worker Queues
ferrox/architectures/queues-jobs.description: Long-running operations (PDF report compilation, video transcoding, external API syncs, batch emails) must never run inside HTTP request handlers.

ferrox/architectures/sagas.title: 🔄 The Saga Pattern (Distributed Transactions)
ferrox/architectures/sagas.description: In a monolithic architecture, you can wrap multiple database operations in a single SQL Transaction (BEGIN; ... COMMIT;). If any operation fails, you simply issue a ROLLBACK.

ferrox/architectures/task-scheduling.title: ⏰ Cron Task Scheduling
ferrox/architectures/task-scheduling.description: Many applications require periodic background tasks—such as clearing expired sessions every night at midnight, recalculating analytics hourly, or polling external feeds every 5 minutes.

ferrox/cli/code-factory.title: 🛠️ The Code Factory
ferrox/cli/code-factory.description: The defining feature of Ferrox is its ability to break the boundary between Backend and Frontend.

ferrox/cli/commands-reference.title: 🛠️ CLI Commands Reference
ferrox/cli/commands-reference.description: cargo-ferrox provides an interactive command-line interface for scaffolding new projects and generating strongly typed TypeScript API clients for frontend applications.

ferrox/community/donations.title: 💖 Support & Donations
ferrox/community/donations.description: First of all, thank you for using and considering supporting Ferrox Framework! 🚀

ferrox/databases/migrations.title: 🔄 Schema Migrations Management
ferrox/databases/migrations.description: As production systems evolve, database schemas require incremental versioning without downtime. ferrox-migrations provides automated schema migrations runner for relational and document databases.

ferrox/databases/mongodb.title: 🍃 Document Databases (MongoDB)
ferrox/databases/mongodb.description: For document-oriented storage, Ferrox provides ferrox-database-mongo, wrapping the official mongodb driver for Rust.

ferrox/databases/overview.title: 💾 Persistence Architecture & Repository Pattern
ferrox/databases/overview.description: In enterprise software development, coupling controllers or business logic directly to raw database queries creates brittle, untestable code.

ferrox/databases/redis.title: 🔴 In-Memory Caching & Redis
ferrox/databases/redis.description: Redis is the standard in-memory storage engine for high-speed session management, caching, distributed locks, rate limiting, and real-time pub/sub.

ferrox/databases/seaorm.title: 🐘 Relational Databases (SeaORM)
ferrox/databases/seaorm.description: For relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite), Ferrox integrates with SeaORM via ferrox-database-seaorm.

ferrox/deployment/ci-cd.title: 🤖 CI/CD Automation & GitHub Actions
ferrox/deployment/ci-cd.description: Automating testing, code quality linting, security vulnerability auditing, and documentation deployment ensures continuous delivery without regressions.

ferrox/deployment/docker-kubernetes.title: 🏭 Production Deployment: Docker & Kubernetes
ferrox/deployment/docker-kubernetes.description: Deploying Rust microservices to production environments requires minimal container sizes, high security isolation (non-root runtimes), fast CI build caching, and Kubernetes deployment manifests.

ferrox/fundamentals/configuration.title: ⚙️ Typed Configuration Management
ferrox/fundamentals/configuration.description: Applications need environment-specific configurations (port numbers, database URLs, JWT secret keys, log levels) that change between Development, Staging, and Production environments.

ferrox/fundamentals/controllers.title: 🕹️ Controllers: The Masterpiece Guide
ferrox/fundamentals/controllers.description: In a Ferrox application, a Controller is the ultimate boundary between the unpredictable outside world (HTTP TCP streams) and the strict, type-safe inner world of your business logic.

ferrox/fundamentals/errors.title: 🚨 Centralized Error Handling & Exception Filters
ferrox/fundamentals/errors.description: Robust applications require predictable, strongly typed error handling. In Ferrox, ferrox-errors provides a centralized AppError enum that implements Axum's IntoResponse trait.

ferrox/fundamentals/interceptors.title: 🔄 Interceptors: Request Execution Pipeline
ferrox/fundamentals/interceptors.description: An Interceptor in Ferrox is a middle layer that wraps handler execution, inspired by NestJS Interceptors and Aspect-Oriented Programming (AOP). Interceptors allow you to inspect, transform, or log incoming HTTP requests and outgoing HTTP responses.

ferrox/fundamentals/middlewares.title: 🔗 Middlewares
ferrox/fundamentals/middlewares.description: Middleware is a function which is called before the route handler. Middleware functions have access to the request and response objects, and the next() middleware function in the application’s request-response cycle.

ferrox/fundamentals/providers.title: 💉 Providers & Dependency Injection
ferrox/fundamentals/providers.description: Providers are a fundamental concept in Ferrox. Many of the basic Ferrox classes may be treated as a provider – services, repositories, factories, helpers, and so on.

ferrox/fundamentals/testing.title: 🧪 Testing & Quality Assurance Strategy
ferrox/fundamentals/testing.description: Testing in enterprise Rust applications must cover multiple levels of isolation: fast unit tests for business logic, in-memory route tests for controllers without binding to network sockets, and ephemeral containerized integration tests for database operations.

ferrox/integrations/feature-flags.title: 🚩 Feature Flags & Toggles
ferrox/integrations/feature-flags.description: Feature flags allow developers to safely roll out new features to a subset of users, perform A/B testing, or instantaneously disable failing endpoints without redeploying code.

ferrox/integrations/i18n.title: 🌐 Internationalization (i18n)
ferrox/integrations/i18n.description: Global enterprise applications require serving localized user interface strings and translated error messages based on the client's Accept-Language HTTP header.

ferrox/integrations/mailer.title: 📧 Email Dispatching (Mailer)
ferrox/integrations/mailer.description: Sending transactional emails (password reset links, account verifications, invoice receipts) is a core requirement for web applications.

ferrox/integrations/notifications.title: 🔔 Notifications & Slack Integration
ferrox/integrations/notifications.description: Real-time developer notifications and DevOps alert dispatching (for server outages, critical errors, or high-value purchase events) require webhook integration with team chat tools.

ferrox/integrations/payments.title: 💳 Payment Gateways (Stripe & Google Pay)
ferrox/integrations/payments.description: Integrating e-commerce payments requires secure checkout session handling and cryptographic signature verification of incoming payment webhooks.

ferrox/integrations/reports-and-cloud.title: 📄 Reports & Cloud Helper Utilities
ferrox/integrations/reports-and-cloud.description: Enterprise business applications often require generating PDF invoices, CSV data exports, and interacting with Cloud SDKs (AWS S3/DynamoDB, GCP Cloud Storage, Azure Blob Storage).

ferrox/integrations/webhooks.title: 🔗 Outgoing Webhook Dispatcher
ferrox/integrations/webhooks.description: When your platform allows external developers to subscribe to API events (e.g. order.created, invoice.paid), sending reliable outgoing webhooks requires cryptographic signing (HMAC-SHA256) and automated retry logic with exponential backoff.

ferrox/observability/health-checks.title: 🩺 Kubernetes Health Probes (Liveness & Readiness)
ferrox/observability/health-checks.description: Container orchestrators like Kubernetes require standardized HTTP endpoints to monitor application health and manage pod lifecycles:

ferrox/observability/logging.title: 📊 Structured Logging & Sentry Integration
ferrox/observability/logging.description: Production observability begins with structured logging. Plain text println! statements are difficult to search in log aggregators like Datadog, Grafana Loki, or AWS CloudWatch.

ferrox/observability/metrics.title: 📈 Prometheus Metrics Export
ferrox/observability/metrics.description: Monitoring real-time application throughput, request latencies, and error rates requires exporting metrics to monitoring platforms like Prometheus and Grafana.

ferrox/observability/tracing.title: 🕵️ OpenTelemetry & Distributed Tracing
ferrox/observability/tracing.description: In a distributed microservice network, a single user HTTP request might pass through an API Gateway, an Authentication service, an Inventory service, and a Payments database.

ferrox/overview.title: Overview
ferrox/overview.description: Ferrox is a high-performance, event-driven backend framework built in Rust. It is designed for maximum throughput, memory safety, and seamless integration with event streaming platforms like Kafka.

ferrox/overview/first-steps.title: 🚀 First Steps: Getting Started
ferrox/overview/first-steps.description: This guide walks you through building your very first Ferrox application from scratch. We will cover environment preparation, application bootstrapping, router setup, and starting the HTTP transport server.

ferrox/overview/introduction.title: 🚀 Introduction
ferrox/overview/introduction.description: Welcome to Ferrox (v0.5.0), a progressive Rust framework for building efficient, reliable, enterprise-grade server-side applications.

ferrox/overview/lifecycle.title: 🔄 Request Lifecycle & Architecture
ferrox/overview/lifecycle.description: To truly understand how Ferrox achieves massive scale and uncompromising security, we must zoom out and look at the "Big Picture".

ferrox/performance/benchmarks.title: ⚡ High-Throughput Benchmarks & Tuning
ferrox/performance/benchmarks.description: Ferrox is designed to process 100,000+ HTTP requests per second per node with sub-millisecond latencies.

ferrox/performance/profiling.title: 🔬 CPU & Memory Profiling (Flamegraphs)
ferrox/performance/profiling.description: Identifying performance bottlenecks, CPU hot paths, and unexpected heap memory allocations in production systems requires low-overhead profiling tools.

ferrox/security/advanced-auth.title: 🔑 Advanced Security: Dual Tokens & PublicId Obfuscation
ferrox/security/advanced-auth.description: Basic JWT authentication often suffers from two enterprise security vulnerabilities:

ferrox/security/circuit-breaker.title: ⚡ Circuit Breakers & Fault Tolerance
ferrox/security/circuit-breaker.description: In distributed microservices, downstream database outages or third-party API latency spikes can exhaust server connection threads, causing cascading failures across your entire infrastructure.

ferrox/security/distributed-locks.title: 🔒 Distributed Synchronization & Locks
ferrox/security/distributed-locks.description: In multi-instance microservice deployments, running background processes or mutating shared resources (e.g., inventory deduction or batch invoice generation) requires cross-process synchronization to prevent race conditions.

ferrox/security/ferrox-selftest.title: 🧪 Ferrox Selftest (Automated Audit & Benchmarks)
ferrox/security/ferrox-selftest.description: ferrox-selftest is the autonomous verification, continuous integration security benchmark runner, and OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG) self-attack auditor for the Ferrox ecosystem.

ferrox/security/ferrox-sentinel.title: 🤖 Ferrox Sentinel (37 SOTA Innovations & Kernel Hardening)
ferrox/security/ferrox-sentinel.description: Ferrox Sentinel (ferrox-sentinel v0.6.0) is an enterprise-grade AI/ML security analytics, threat detection, and kernel defense mesh built directly into the Ferrox framework.

ferrox/security/jwt.title: 🔒 Zero-Trust & Dual JWT
ferrox/security/jwt.description: Ferrox adopts a Zero-Trust security posture by default. This means that every single HTTP request, even internal ones coming from other microservices, is treated as hostile until proven valid.

ferrox/security/rate-limiting.title: 🛡️ Rate Limiting & Throttling
ferrox/security/rate-limiting.description: To protect APIs from abuse, credential stuffing attacks, and Denial of Service (DoS), Ferrox provides ferrox-rate-limiter—a Redis-backed rate limiting engine implementing atomic fixed-window and token-bucket algorithms.

ferrox/security/singleflight.title: 🚀 Singleflight: Cache Stampede Protection
ferrox/security/singleflight.description: When a high-traffic cache key expires (e.g. homepage top products or hot news stories), hundreds or thousands of concurrent incoming HTTP requests simultaneously miss the cache and hit the primary database.

ferrox/transports/datagrid.title: 📊 Enterprise DataGrid Query Translators
ferrox/transports/datagrid.description: Enterprise admin dashboards rely on rich frontend data grid libraries like AG Grid, MUI X DataGrid, and TanStack Table. These grids send complex URL query parameters containing filtering, multi-column sorting, page sizes, and search constraints.

ferrox/transports/file-storage.title: 📁 File Upload & Storage Abstractions
ferrox/transports/file-storage.description: Handling user file uploads (profile avatars, document attachments, media assets) requires decoupled storage backends that can switch seamlessly between local filesystem storage in development and S3/MinIO cloud object storage in production.

ferrox/transports/graphql.title: 🕸️ GraphQL API Integration
ferrox/transports/graphql.description: GraphQL allows frontend clients to request precisely the data fields they need, reducing over-fetching and network payload sizes.

ferrox/transports/graphql-advanced.title: 🚀 Advanced GraphQL: DataLoader & Subscriptions
ferrox/transports/graphql-advanced.description: Standard GraphQL query resolvers suffer from the infamous N+1 Query Problem. If a client fetches a list of 100 posts along with their authors, a naive resolver fires 1 initial query for posts plus 100 individual database queries for each author (101 total DB roundtrips!).

ferrox/transports/sse.title: 📡 Server-Sent Events (SSE)
ferrox/transports/sse.description: For real-time, unidirectional server-to-client data streaming (such as live stock price ticks, progress bars, or AI text streaming responses like ChatGPT), Server-Sent Events (SSE) provide a lightweight HTTP-native protocol.

ferrox/transports/transports-overview.title: 🌐 Multi-Transport Application System
ferrox/transports/transports-overview.description: Most traditional web frameworks only support HTTP REST servers out of the box. Enterprise backend applications, however, often need to run multiple server protocols simultaneously—for example, an HTTP REST API server on port 3000, a gRPC microservice server on port 50051, and an FTP or WebSocket file server.

ferrox/tutorial/building-the-core.title: 🏗️ Part 2: Building the Core
ferrox/tutorial/building-the-core.description: Now that our application is running, let's implement the core logic for our Ticketing System following the "Thin Controllers, Fat Providers" best practice.

ferrox/tutorial/code-factory.title: 🤖 Part 3: The Code Factory
ferrox/tutorial/code-factory.description: Our Backend is solid, but writing the exact same interfaces and API calls manually in TypeScript for the Frontend is an anti-pattern that leads to massive synchronization bugs.

ferrox/tutorial/setup.title: 🚀 Part 1: Project Setup
ferrox/tutorial/setup.description: Welcome to the Ferrox Zero-to-Hero Tutorial.

nestjs-yalc/architecture.title: Architecture
nestjs-yalc/architecture.description: NestJS-YALC is structured as a modular monorepo, providing a bridge between raw Node.js utilities and the NestJS dependency injection system.

nestjs-yalc/modules/crud-gen.title: CRUD Generator
nestjs-yalc/modules/crud-gen.description: The @nest-yalc-2/crud-gen module is a powerful code generator that automates the creation of REST controllers and GraphQL resolvers based directly on your TypeORM entities.

nestjs-yalc/modules/logger.title: Logger
nestjs-yalc/modules/logger.description: The @nest-yalc-2/logger module provides a high-performance, Pino-based logging infrastructure for NestJS applications. It automatically correlates HTTP requests, Redacts sensitive information, and integrates seamlessly with OpenTelemetry for distributed tracing.

nestjs-yalc/overview.title: Overview
nestjs-yalc/overview.description: NestJS-YALC (Yet Another Library Collection) is an enterprise-grade library suite designed specifically for NestJS 11+ and TypeScript 6+. It extends the core NestJS framework with a collection of pre-built, production-ready modules that address the most common and complex challenges in enterprise backend development.

node-yalc/overview.title: Overview
node-yalc/overview.description: Node-YALC is the pure Node.js/TypeScript foundation of the YALC ecosystem. Unlike nestjs-yalc, which is tightly coupled to the NestJS dependency injection and module system, node-yalc provides framework-agnostic utilities, types, and base classes that can be used in any Node.js environment.
